record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can knowledge exchange add and merge source data into a target knowledge base that is already populated, when inference in knowledge bases is complex and practical solutions also need deduplication, record linkage, same-as links, and conflict resolution for values?

evidence.quote: An interesting open problem is to understand how to do this in KBs where inference is more complex. In addition, practical solutions will need to use deduplication and record linkage to create links such as same-as and resolve conflicts in values.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a knowledge base (KB) be a pair K = (I, Σ), where I is an instance (a finite set of ground facts over a relational/ontological signature) and Σ is a set of logical sentences (constraints and inference rules, e.g., tuple-generating dependencies, equality-generating dependencies, or description-logic axioms) under which the certain answers (or chase-closure) of K are defined. A source KB K_S = (I_S, Σ_S) and a target KB K_T = (I_T, Σ_T) are given, together with a schema mapping M = (Σ_ST) consisting of source-to-target dependencies. A knowledge exchange solution is a target instance J extending I_T such that (J, Σ_T) together with (I_S, Σ_ST) satisfies all dependencies, while preserving the certain-answer semantics with respect to a chosen query language.

Classical knowledge exchange assumes that the target instance I_T is empty and that Σ_T is restricted (e.g., to dependencies admitting a terminating chase). The problem is to develop a theory and algorithms for knowledge exchange in the general setting where:

(a) the target KB is already populated, i.e., I_T ≠ ∅, and may contain facts that overlap with or conflict with material induced from I_S via M;
(b) Σ_T expresses richer inference (for instance, full first-order constraints, expressive description logics such as members of the DL-Lite, EL, or SHIQ families, or existential rules beyond known decidable fragments);
(c) the construction of J must incorporate deduplication and record linkage, producing same-as (owl:sameAs-style) links that identify co-referent constants/individuals between I_S and I_T; and
(d) value-level conflicts between facts in I_T and facts derived from I_S must be resolved by an explicit conflict-resolution policy.

Formalize the notion of a "merging solution" J in this setting (existence, universality, and certain-answer preservation under M and Σ_T), characterize the complexity of computing such a solution and of answering queries over it, and provide algorithms that simultaneously perform chase-based materialization, entity resolution (production of same-as links), and value-conflict resolution while remaining sound and complete with respect to the chosen semantics.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in knowledge exchange: extending classical (empty-target) knowledge exchange to populated target KBs with rich inference, while integrating record linkage and conflict resolution. No comprehensive solution unifying these aspects appears in the literature; related work addresses pieces (entity resolution, conflict-resolution in data fusion, knowledge-base exchange under DL-Lite) but not the combined problem.

status_evidence.title: Knowledge Base Exchange: The Case of OWL 2 QL
status_evidence.snippet: Studies knowledge base exchange under DL-Lite with empty target, leaving populated-target and richer DLs as future work.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work on knowledge exchange addresses restricted settings, not populated targets with combined deduplication/conflict resolution.
